auditor: separate assistant agent; not human adjudication
scope: 13 page_excerpt records only; no historical_search revalidation and no synthetic assessment; no access to held-out samples
retrievalMethod: web.open on every exact URL; cached/indexed renderings supplied by the web tool, not a guaranteed fresh origin-server snapshot
limitations: This audit establishes observable provenance on 2026-11-18; it does not retroactively prove browsing took place on 2026-11-17.
Labels reflect the reviewed page, whereas the evaluator sees only a hand-selected title and tiny excerpt. Missing genre evidence in that input is not proof the page is not a review.
No human gold labels, held-out status, representative sampling or online quality claim is introduced by this audit.
Bibliographically compatible and different release are weaker than an exact ISBN/edition verification.
Most of the copied strings are bibliographic metadata. Four inputs concatenate nonadjacent fields; call them selected excerpt segments, not one contiguous quotation or provider response.
Rucer initial retrieval succeeded, but later tail/find retrievals timed out; full-page verification is not claimed.
recommendations: Keep PR86 inputs and original result immutable when comparing rules; add this audit separately so provenance corrections are explicit.
Treat work identity, visible genre evidence and edition clues as distinct. A positive whole-page label can coexist with genre unknown on the small search-like input.
Keep the two uncertain records excluded from binary precision/recall unless an explicit annotation policy resolves them.
Do not infer publisher/catalog versus independent review purely from the identical title/author/ISBN subset; omitted page context matters.

records.notes: Visible article gives first-person assessment of the target work. Publication month/publisher match the reference fields; exact ISBN is not printed in the selected evidence.
Signed reading commentary evaluates this work and describes the reader's response; it is not a Q&A with the book author. The selected input supplies only identity fields, omitting evaluative prose.

Body is an interview with Lan Xiaohuan. The words Shanghai Book Review identify the section/interviewer, not the document genre. The retained excerpt is present in the first successful open at line 28; a later find missed the same string.
Bibliographic catalog, with title, author, publisher and matching ISBN. The input combines nonadjacent fields and omits the catalog heading/context.

Initial open shows a brief personal evaluation followed by a long extracts section. Review-versus-notebook policy remains unresolved. Subsequent attempts to retrieve the end of the article or find the heading timed out.

Signed analytical reading essay centered on the target work, compatible with the broad work-commentary label. Under a narrower critical-review-only definition this should be adjudicated. Its selected input is a bibliographic caption and does not itself establish genre. Caption lists only Chen Jian as translator; another audited source describes co-translation with Liu Chang, so it is not a complete edition authority.
Explicit interview with the author; multiple works/academic biography are discussed. Author portrait caption is present. No target edition identity established.
Main reviewed work is Ru Lin Da Di, not the target Soulstealers. Soulstealers is discussed comparatively, including criticism; that does not make this a focused review of it.

Translator's remembrance covers translation and publication history plus evaluations of two works. Its author is connected to the translated work. Keep uncertain rather than turn it into an independent-review gold positive.

Article is a full Kirkus review of Kidder's work. Initial open displayed only the template/teaser; opening near line 124 exposed title, author, 1981 release and review text. This supports different-release from the reference 2000 paperback, not textual edition equivalence.

Publisher product page has title, author, 2000 sale date, paperback format, target ISBN, retailer buttons and marketing text quoting review blurbs. Those quotations do not make this an independent review. The input combines nonadjacent metadata.

Signed review contains extended interpretation of Scott's work and implications for arts grantmakers. Bibliography cites Yale, 1998; reference paperback is 1999. different_release is a publication-date distinction, not proof of differing contents or exact ISBN identity. Input skips the intervening bibliography line.

Publisher product page prints target ISBN and 1999 paperback date plus buy links and review blurbs. It is not an original independent review. Input combines author and ISBN fields separated by other metadata.
